Blocked by TaskPacket path restrictions. The flashlight example is located at `examples/flashlight/run.py`, but the packet only allows edits under `src/`, `tests/`, and `.control-tower/`. No product code was changed.

Implemented gamepad flashlight toggle support in `examples/flashlight/run.py`. The new `--toggle-key` CLI argument defaults to `Gamepad_FaceButton_Right`, leaving the existing pose capture default `Gamepad_FaceButton_Top` unchanged.
Add gamepad flashlight toggle in example
Update repo docs after Builder work

Updated examples/flashlight/run.py so gamepad flashlight toggling uses IsInputKeyDown edge detection polled at 60 Hz instead of relying on WasInputKeyJustPressed at the idle interval. The default toggle key remains Gamepad_FaceButton_Right, which maps to Xbox B. The same edge pattern is applied to the gamepad pose capture key while preserving Enter terminal capture.

Flashlight polling is using IsInputKeyDown edge detection for the toggle key and controller capture key, with polling capped at 60 Hz so normal Xbox B presses are not missed. The default toggle remains Unreal Gamepad_FaceButton_Right, which maps to Xbox B. The previous failure mode was coarse polling at the idle period, where a normal short button press could occur entirely between polls and never be observed.

Fixed examples/flashlight/run.py so the flashlight and capture controller polling no longer constructs FKey via game.get_unreal_object(uclass='FKey'). The code now passes an FKey-shaped struct argument ({"KeyName": key_name}) directly to APlayerController.IsInputKeyDown, allowing SPEAR's function-call struct deserialization path to handle FKey.
